fingerprint.fps: variable, 30 nominal; 17099 video frames in 910.37 s

interventions.what: Bandicam window capture of the Isle Wars Pro game window; the owner played one game from the options screen to the end screen (15:10 recording). The video file is the only output. No scripted clicks. Counters, seats and screens were read from pixels by region comparison and template matching of glyph shapes, with no OCR pass.

start_state.restore: Owner launched a new game on the unregistered Pro build from the options screen (seat 1 human, three computer seats, starting level set to the easy entry and game speed to the slow entry). Pro has no save file (C-SET-05), so no state was restored. The recording starts on the title screen; the opening deal is the first board.

args: probe: 910.37 s, 17099 video frames, variable frame rate (nominal 30), 1920x1080 H.264, AAC 48 kHz stereo, 103171810 bytes
ffmpeg 8.0.1; the panel regions were read frame by frame from the container timestamps; offsets are mm:ss.mmm video offsets
record content: the event message, the army totals, the seat eliminations, the concession offer, how the human won, and the scoreboard before and after its update

observations.field: event scan over the whole video
observations.value: the middle panel was scanned at 4 frames a second for the pink message text and the hits checked against the turn they fell in; one event message in 29 turns, between turns and of the production-centre increase kind (04:16.50 to 04:23.00, between turn 12 green and turn 13 blue; the middle panel at 04:19.0 shows its text); none before turn 12; 1 of the 26 turn changes from turn 4 on, about 4 per cent (the setting was the middle one). Across the four sittings 8 of 157 changes (IP1 026: 2 of 49, IP1 027: 3 of 40, IP1 028: 2 of 42, here 1 of 26).

observations.field: army totals: how they are read
observations.value: the sum of the readable country counters of each colour at a moment between two attacks; one country (46) could not be assigned a colour in some frames and is left out (at most 4 armies), so totals are lower bounds by that country; the sums are armies on the board. The totals at 13:50.0 show one red country (1 army) read from a flash after the scoreboard had already read 0 for red.

observations.field: territory counts: the human seat's path
observations.value: blue 14 at the deal; 15 to 16 until 03:46; 18 at 03:46; 20 at 05:15; 24 at 07:26; 29 at 11:09; 31 at 12:51; 32 at 13:23; 33 at 13:34.03 (first frame at 33); 35 at 13:50; 40 at 14:29.3; 41 at 14:48.8 (the last human capture, yellow's last country). The seats were eliminated: red at 13:50.07 (the human's attack 48, cards 4 to 0 seven seconds later), yellow at 14:48.8 (attack 54); green kept 5 countries. Yellow's three cards were still on the scoreboard at the end (14:58.5), the elimination of a seat at the last attack of a turn not yet clearing them.

observations.field: the end: the concession offer and the order of events
observations.value: the human held 33 countries from 13:34.03 and went on attacking for 75 more seconds in the same turn (turn 29, 12:56.7 to 14:48.8), taking 8 more countries; the turn ended with the draw screen (14:54.5 hand with the shield card, a draw); the offer came at the turn transition, a banner of two buttons (accept, play on) with a dialog saying that the computer seats concede to the blue seat, from about 14:55.0 to 15:01.2 (scene changes at 14:54.93 and 14:55.03); as in IP1 028 the offer came at the end of the human turn that held 33 or more, not at the 33rd capture (here 75 s and 8 countries later); the owner pressed the accept button, which brightens at 15:01.0, and both buttons were gone by 15:01.4.

observations.field: the end: winner dialog, scoreboard, title
observations.value: a dialog named the blue seat the winner from 15:01.47 (scene change at 15:01.47) to 15:03.77; the scoreboard screen came at 15:03.77 (rows for three levels: won, lost, percent) and read, for the three rows, easy 0 won 0 lost 0 %, normal 1 won 3 lost 0 % at 15:04.0; at 15:06.13 the screen changed: easy 1 won 0 lost 100 %, normal 1 won 3 lost 25 % (frame at 15:06.0 already shows the new numbers within a rounding of the scene-change time, the frame at 15:06.1 to 15:06.2 is the first with them); the title screen at about 15:08.0; the recording ends at 15:10.4 on the title screen. The game just won was played on the easy level and appears in the easy row (1 won, 0 lost); the normal row is 1 won, 3 lost: the three earlier losses (IP1 025 to 027) and one win, which fits IP1 028's accepted win (a normal-level game). So the win of a concession is recorded; the scoreboard first shows the old numbers and updates 2.4 s after it appears.

observations.field: the scoreboard of IP1 028, looked at again with this video in hand
observations.value: IP1 028's scoreboard screen was up for 2.0 s only (18:19.03 to 18:21.03) and showed normal 0 won, 3 lost; the update seen here comes 2.4 s after the screen appears, so the owner left that screen before it; that sitting's note that no win was shown is explained by the timing (the next screen at its start, normal 1 won 3 lost, shows the win recorded). Written as a note in CORRECTIONS.md; E018-r0013 stays as written (rule 20).

observations.field: the end: the owner won
observations.value: the human (blue) seat won by accepting the concession at 15:01.2, holding 41 of 46 countries (green 5, yellow and red 0); 29 player-turns (8 human, 21 computer) from 00:48.2 to 14:54.5; the human turns lasted 33 s to 110 s, computer turns 3 to 10 s (the longer of them: 8.2 s); the owner played the easy level at slow speed
